newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Franc Zone bank head says Ghana, Guinea welcome.
newsitem.headline: Franc Zone bank head says Ghana, Guinea welcome.

text.p: Charles Konan Banny, governor of the Central Bank of West African States (BCEAO), said Guinea and even Ghana would be welcome to join the Franc Zone.
The zone groups France, its dependencies, Monaco, the Comoro Islands and 14 other African states grouped in two blocs. The Africans all use variants of the CFA franc.
The Portuguese-speaking West African state of Guinea-Bissau converts fully to the CFA franc on August 1.
Asked by Ivory Coast daily Fraternite-Matin whether other countries might join the Zone, Banny said Guinea would be welcome.
"The same for Ghana, why not? Ghana is a very important country for us," he said in an interview published on Tuesday.
Guinea had once been indifferent, but certain sections of society were showing more interest now, he said.
"We spoke about it openly to the highest authorities in Guinea the last time I was there," Banny said.

The BCEAO is the central bank of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (UEMOA). Banny said he would like to extend membership of UEMOA to all the members of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS).
ECOWAS, which includes Ghana and Nigeria, is a wider grouping than UEMOA, but is much less advanced in terms of being a free trade zone or economic union.

Banny said language was not a barrier, as the membership of Guinea-Bissau showed, and that the main requirement was to share "the ideal of integration, of a common monetary policy, of economic integration".
Spanish-speaking Equatorial Guinea has been a member since 1985.
He said the central bank of Guinea-Bissau had become a national office of the BCEAO, which is based in Dakar, Senegal.
